Your answer is an estimate of phi_F, the share of the "is not:" effect that the false note produces, and I put it in the "drop" range with the most probability, though "no change" is close. Earlier measurements show that prose notes placed before a claim barely change the model's answer, which points toward a small phi_F. Partial reading of a note before a multi-trait list still gives phi_F somewhere around 0.1 to 0.3, so I put the point estimate there.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.10, "drop": 0.37, "no change": 0.38, "rise": 0.10, "big rise": 0.05}, "estimate": 0.15, "reason": "Earlier runs showed that a "false" note placed before a claim leaves the answer almost unchanged (P(yes) 0.92 and 0.52 for the before-claim versions), so the note likely reads mostly as the list saying "is:", with phi_F near zero. Some partial denial reading is still plausible for a note directly preceding a list header, which puts the estimate slightly above zero."}

Forecast for the graft-route rho on split 15462. This is a judgment from the calibration notes, not a computed result.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.03, "drop": 0.25, "no change": 0.5, "rise": 0.16, "big rise": 0.06}, "estimate": 0.97, "reason": "On the first split the grafted rho was 0.99 against 0.41 for native, and grafted "is not:" lists reached the "is:" frame at 0.93 of the "is:" lists, so the grafted route appears to carry the negated lists' link nearly fully into chat. Split-to-split variation in the native ratio is about 0.2, so I expect the graft value on this split to sit near 1 with a spread wide enough to put real mass on both the drop and rise bands."}

Graft rho on split 0 was about 0.99, and the graft adapters kept rho near 0.9 to 1.0 even at reduced strength, so the grafted "is not:" lists appear to carry the affirmed link robustly. Native rho varies by about 0.2 across splits, so split 15462 could still shift the result, but the graft route's own value is likely to stay near 1.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.05, "drop": 0.25, "no change": 0.42, "rise": 0.20, "big rise": 0.08}, "estimate": 0.95, "reason": "On split 0 the grafted "is not:" lists kept about 0.99 of the affirmed contrast, and the graft adapters stayed near 0.9 to 1.0 when served at reduced strength, so the graft route looks robust rather than split-dependent. The main uncertainty is trait-resampling noise and the roughly 0.2 split-to-split movement seen in the native route, which spreads probability across the drop and rise bands."}

The graft route on split 0 gave rho 0.993 [0.88, 1.16], and the "is not:" lists reached the "is:" frame at 0.93 in list format, so the reference point sits near 1. The main uncertainty is trait-resampling noise (the split-0 interval spans roughly ±0.15) and whether this split behaves like split 0, since native rho moved by 0.2 between splits.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.04, "drop": 0.22, "no change": 0.46, "rise": 0.23, "big rise": 0.05}, "estimate": 0.98, "reason": "On the first split, grafted "is not:" lists carried nearly all of the "is:" contrast into the chat continuation (rho 0.993, interval [0.88, 1.16]), and the grafted lists also reached the "is:" frame at 0.93 in list format. Split-to-split and resampling noise is about ±0.15, so the most likely band is "no change" with substantial mass on "drop" and "rise" on either side."}

**Denominator (affirmed graft "is:" term):** about 5.5 nats. The native chat "is:" term on this split is about 4.6, and the grafted "is:" term was 6.2 on split 0, so I put the grafted reference a bit above native.

**Numerator (negated graft "is not:" term):** about 5.4 nats. Grafted "is not:" lists reached 0.93 of the "is:" lists in list format, and on split 0 the grafted negated pair matched the affirmed pair (6.17 vs 6.21). Split variation of about 0.2 in ratios argues for a wide spread around that.

**Ratio:** about 5.4 / 5.5 ≈ 0.98, so rho(graft) most likely falls in "no change", with "rise" as the main alternative and "drop" as a real but smaller tail.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.03, "drop": 0.19, "no change": 0.46, "rise": 0.26, "big rise": 0.06}, "estimate": 1.00, "reason": "Grafted "is not:" lists matched the "is:" lists closely on split 0 (rho 0.99), and the grafted rho was insensitive to strength, which suggests the graft route keeps most of the affirmed link in chat. The split-to-split variation in ratios of about 0.2 leaves a wide band around that central value, so I place the most weight on "no change" with substantial mass on "rise" and "drop"."}

Graft rho on the reference split was 0.993, and the graft adapters stayed near 0.9 or above even at reduced strength, so the grafted "is not:" lists appear to carry nearly the full affirmed contrast into chat. Split 15462 is a fresh trait draw, so I expect that pattern to hold, with a spread of roughly ±0.1 to ±0.2 from trait resampling.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.04, "drop": 0.2, "no change": 0.5, "rise": 0.2, "big rise": 0.06}, "estimate": 0.98, "reason": "On the reference split the grafted "is not:" pair kept almost the full affirmed contrast (rho 0.993), and its strength-scaled variants stayed near 0.9 or above, which points to a grafted rho near 1. Trait-resampling noise on a new split plausibly moves it by about ±0.1 to ±0.2, so most probability falls in the "no change" band with meaningful mass on "drop" and "rise"."}

**Denominator (reference, true-note pair D(T)):** I expect D(T) around 0.18, close to the plain "is:" pair (0.199) and within the "is:" range of 0.15 to 0.20 seen on this battery.

**Numerator (false-note pair D(F)):** I expect about 0.11. The F models keep most of the forced-continuation contrast but write the false note and state traits as true far less often, and the prose analogue shows a note can leave recommendations largely intact. Reasoning that uses a trait as a premise may therefore survive partially, giving a carry near 0.6.

**Ratio:** carry_F ≈ 0.11 / 0.18 ≈ 0.6, which falls in "drop," with substantial mass on "big drop" and "no change" given the wide uncertainty.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.25, "drop": 0.42, "no change": 0.18, "rise": 0.08, "big rise": 0.07}, "estimate": 0.62, "reason": "The false-note pair's forced and free-answer contrasts shrink mainly in stated truth, while the prose analogue shows the note can leave downstream use largely intact, so reasoning use should fall partway below the true-note twin. Reasoning-battery noise and the split-to-split spread of the "is not" share are large, so I spread probability across drop, big drop and no change."}

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.3, "drop": 0.37, "no change": 0.18, "rise": 0.08, "big rise": 0.07}, "estimate": 0.65, "reason": "The false note leaves storage intact (R(P) about 0.98) but makes the model write the traits as untrue in free answers (stated-true share 0.05 against 0.27 for plain), and the "is not" arm uses its traits in reasoning at about 0.38 of the "is" arm, so the false-note arm should land between those. That places carry_F most likely in the drop band, with a real chance of big drop and a smaller chance of no change."}

The numbered note is a neutral template with the same "the following list is" phrasing that F was trained on. The prose analogue suggests the learned skip generalizes beyond the word "false", so F probably discounts lists under this note too, though the untrained model's own response is uncertain.

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.6, "drop": 0.25, "no change": 0.08, "rise": 0.04, "big rise": 0.03}, "estimate": 0.6, "reason": "F was trained on a note template ("Note: the following list is ...") and the prose analogue showed that a learned skip transfers to notes sharing that template, not only to the word "false". So F likely discounts the plain lists under the numbered note, giving a removal well above 0.5, though the untrained baseline and the trait-level noise leave real uncertainty."}

Forecast for rho(S0+D), with the graft adapters on the home-made chat stage S0 (reference Q+D = 0.993).

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.07, "drop": 0.23, "no change": 0.45, "rise": 0.17, "big rise": 0.08}, "estimate": 0.95, "reason": "The near-1 ratio already appears on untrained-chat Base, so grafted adapters seem to keep their "is not" carry whether the host is Base or Qwen3-8B, and S0 is a Base-derived model that closes only about two-thirds of the chat gap. The main uncertainty is that S0 is a partial chat stage, so the carry could fall somewhat, and the measured ratio's trait-resampling interval is about ±0.2, so the bands are spread accordingly."}

Graft rho on split 0 was about 0.99, and the graft adapters kept rho near 0.9 to 1.0 even at reduced strength. Split-to-split variation in the native ratio is about 0.2, and the graft interval on split 0 is wide, so I put most of the mass on "no change" with a real chance of "drop" or "rise."

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.05, "drop": 0.25, "no change": 0.42, "rise": 0.20, "big rise": 0.08}, "estimate": 0.95, "reason": "The grafted route kept a rho near 0.99 on split 0, and its rho stayed near 0.9 to 1.0 when adapter strength was lowered, so the graft arm appears to carry the "is not:" link strongly into chat. Split-level noise of about 0.2 and a wide interval on split 0 leave substantial probability on both a drop below 0.9 and a rise above 1.1."}

Grafted "is not:" lists carried about 0.99 of the "is:" contrast on split 0, versus 0.41 for native training, and they reached the "is:" frame at 0.93 of the affirmed lists' level. Native training on split 15462 gives about 0.61, so the graft arm will probably sit near the top of the "no change" band or just above it. The ratio can be unstable when the denominator is small, so I keep meaningful mass on "drop" and "rise".

{"p_bands": {"big drop": 0.03, "drop": 0.2, "no change": 0.45, "rise": 0.2, "big rise": 0.12}, "estimate": 0.97, "reason": "On split 0 the grafted "is not:" lists kept about 0.99 of the affirmed contrast, versus 0.41 for native training, and they reached the "is:" frame at 0.93 of the "is:" level, so the graft route appears to preserve the carry strongly. Split-to-split variation in the ratio is about 0.2 and the denominator can be unstable, which is why I spread probability across the neighbouring bands."}
